title: Corruption trial, ICC warrant: Why Netanyahu will stay in politics even if he loses
gist: Al-Monitor analysis: senior Likud figures refuse to contemplate Netanyahu's defeat on Oct. 27, and Netanyahu, 77 with no groomed successor, is likely to remain in politics even if he loses, with his corruption trial and ICC warrant at stake.

insights.claim: Netanyahu is likely to stay in politics even if he loses the Oct. 27 election, since no one in Likud will contemplate his defeat and he has never groomed a successor.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: A Netanyahu loss does not imply a clean transition; Likud turmoil and continued opposition leadership are likely.
insights.locator: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is likely to stay

insights.claim: Polls suggest Netanyahu could face a deadlock with Gadi Eisenkot or even a humiliating defeat, yet Likud figures remain convinced he will prevail as in nearly every election over 17 years.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Polls versus Likud confidence: outcome uncertainty is high.

insights.claim: Netanyahu stands to lose more than the premiership: his criminal corruption trial and the ICC arrest warrant against him are also at stake.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Personal legal incentives drive his behavior, including possible escalation or coalition choices.

insights.claim: A senior Likud minister said anyone trying to push Netanyahu aside 'will be punished', and that he will leave when he wants to.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.quote: Anyone who tries to push him aside will be punished.
insights.locator: Asked why no one in the party
